chapter: Records, Jimmy Wade and Richard M. Jones
title: Richard M. Jones and the Session company records
summary: Punch recalls records with Jones before leaving Chicago.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: Met him in New York or in California? No, New York. I see. Did you ever know Richard M Jones?

Yeah, I made records with him. Richard M Jones, crippled fellow. Yeah, played piano. Where did you make the records with him? And John had none of them records? Man, I made plenty of records with Richard M Jones. No, I don't have any of the ones you made with him. Mr. Bill didn't have none? He probably does, somewhere hidden. He must be got them records. Man, all his own stuff though, you know, he was writing out his stuff himself, you know. He could write out some nice stuff boy, Richard M Jones. Yeah, crippled fellow. I worked with him in Chicago.
You played jobs with him, spot jobs? Yeah, but you know, not gigs I mean, not going to run one steady job. You remember he was in the band with you with Richard M Jones,
either tuned or? Boy, them things would get me, look like my mind
Yeah. I'd come left over that, you know. Well, by what time was that when you were working

with Richard M Jones? Well, this was near a time when I was fixing to leave Chicago. A little time before I joined them shows, you know, and cut out of Chicago. A little before that, I was working on that way with him. Did you know a white guy named Phil Featheringale up there? Featheringale, I heard of that name many times, but I don't believe I knew him. Yeah. Yeah.
I'm trying to figure out which records you made, you know, and all that. Because I know you made some records for one of those companies. I think it was a Session company or something.
Session, yeah. That was downtown Chicago. Yeah, but that's the guy I said went away, and I never could get no royalties or nothing from him.
That must be Phil Feathering. Yeah, yeah. And those are the same ones with Richard M. Jones? Or was that...
I'll be to some other company. I know it was because we went to different places to make them records.

Well, hold a minute and see if I can find this book. And this was Richard M. Jones you made records with just before you left Chicago. Yeah. And you don't remember the guys in the band or anything yet?
No, that's what I asked you. I thought the name was in there.
